findings.rationale: Accept the original separate human-footprinting comparison. evidence.quote: At a specific CTCF binding site on chromosome 1, we observed a clear footprint (a deep notch of ATAC-seq signal), similar to footprints seen by DNase-seq25,26, at the precise location of the CTCF motif that coincides with the summit of the CTCF ChIP-seq signal in GM12878 cells (Fig 4a).

Using genomic DNaseI footprinting across 41 diverse cell and tissue types, we detected 45 million factor occupancy events within regulatory regions, representing differential binding to 8.4 million distinct short sequence elements.
Briefly, roughly 10 million cells were grown in appropriate culture media and nuclei were extracted using NP-40 in an isotonic buffer.
The small ‘double-hit’ fragments (<500 bp) were recovered by sucrose ultra-centrifugation, endrepaired and ligated with adapters compatible with the Illumina sequencing platform.
High quality libraries from each cell type were sequenced on the Illumina platform to an average depth of 273 million uniquely mapping single-end tags.

While only a subset of these motif instances (2,351) coincided with high-confidence footprints, the vast majority of NRF1 motif instances in DNaseI footprints (89%) overlapped reproducible NRF1 ChIP-seq peaks (Fig. 1c).

summary: Independently reviewed all 14 original claims against the registered seed citation contexts and the cited works themselves. All 14 are accepted as written at their existing qualified scope; none is silently revised. All 32 unresolved items have individual zero-based assessments and retain their original wording. The seed and R5/R11/R13/R14/R16/R23/R24/R26 are primary full texts; R4/R10/R12/R18/R19/R25 are primary abstracts. The bibliography establishes citation identity/context only, and catalogue records establish candidate identities only. No direct whole-assay ancestor or admitted catalogue merge is established. R11 supports explicit adoption of coupled Tn5 fragmentation/adapter tagging with PCR-compatible output, not complete reagent/interface equivalence, inheritance of every recovery choice or a component-isolated gain. R10 is a narrower hyperactive-Tn5 biochemical precedent; R12 is a Hermes/yeast in vivo accessibility precedent; R19 and R24 are qualified physical/readout precedents. R4/R5 are background/locus context, and R18 remains condensation background only: its primary abstract does not verify the seed-attributed nuclease-resistant-fragment experiment. R13, R14 and R16 retain distinct DNase protocol, FAIRE benchmark and FAIRE validation scopes; R23 has an explicitly attributed MNase dataset; R25/R26 remain separate qualitative footprint comparisons. Input quantities are protocol recommendations, not universal minima; R13 explicitly permits lower inputs and R16 permits shorter incubations. Reported performance remains attached to its experiment and comparator; author explanations about losses, efficiency, steric accessibility and overdigestion are not upgraded to measured causal gains. All 154 catalogue records were examined by description and reference identity. R4 has a DNase candidate and R14/R16 have FAIRE-side candidates in the joint FAIRE/Sono entry. No catalogue match is forced for external Tn5, shotgun-tagmentation, Hermes, compaction or distinct footprinting contributions. The existing seed extraction is unchanged; only op_tagmentation and op_purify_amplify are used, with no invented before-side or sequencing/analysis operations. The nomination and disposition audit found no omitted nominated candidate: each of the 14 has its own finding. Previously flagged R6/R7 phasing, R8 histone profiling and R21 compaction remain possible follow-up leads with no registered primary papers; their bibliography/catalogue mentions cannot establish new demonstrated relations. The R35 caption-versus-SELEX bibliographic discrepancy remains an unresolved application-data attribution, not evidence of an omitted assay ancestor. No agents were spawned, no network was used, and no input, source, code outside this attempt, or other attempt was modified.
